correctness.rationale: Every nonempty complete binary prefix code with k leaves is an ordered full binary tree, counted by the Catalan recurrence and separately by iterated leaf expansion. Two independent exact decision procedures (reachable subset BFS and backwards pair-coalescence) agree on every tree for sizes 2–9. The 4 exceptional nine-leaf sets have length gcd one and explicit closed nonmerge pair certificates checked transition-by-transition. Pairwise mergeability is necessary and sufficient for decoder synchronization, with any singleton image brought to root by zero-child paths. Finite exhaustive proof only; no extrapolation beyond nine.

value.rationale: A necessary coprimality condition on all codeword lengths is not sufficient for error-recovery synchronization. The first cardinality where this fails and all exceptional labeled codebooks sharpen the meaningful boundary of a published two-length theorem and classify the smallest affected complete binary decoders. The finite classification has concrete value for decoder-code design despite not giving infinite parameters or performance gains.
